title: Bohol International Marathon 2026 Review: Flat, Lit Course and Local Lechon Aid Stations
meta_description: Bohol International Marathon 2026 review: August 30 in Panglao -- a mostly flat, midnight-start course with lechon aid stations, per runner recaps.
dek: Set for 30 August 2026 in Panglao, Bohol, this marathon starts shortly after midnight over a course that's roughly 80% lit, with runner recaps describing well-paved, pothole-free roads and Sandugo Festival-style lechon at aid stations.
verdict: The Bohol International Marathon benefits from genuine, if dated, participant feedback: a 2018 finisher described the Panglao-Dauis roads as well-paved with no potholes and largely flat, especially in the early dark hours, though the same runner also flagged unclear signage for post-race entitlements and said the event 'wasn't the run in paradise' expected. The 2025 edition drew around 4,300 runners using a GPS-tracking app so supporters could follow progress, and aid stations have served local delicacies like lechon alongside standard hydration -- a distinctive Bohol touch. Recent editions lean on promotional coverage more than independent reviews, so treat the flat, well-organised reputation as reasonably reliable but not fully current.

sections.heading: A Flat, Mostly Dark-Hours Course
paragraphs: The course runs mainly along Panglao and Dauis roads. A 2018 finisher's race recap on Takbo.ph described it plainly: "The roads were all well paved. No potholes," [1] and noted the course appears largely flat, especially during the pre-dawn hours. For 2026, a travel-agency preview notes the marathon starts shortly after midnight, with about 80% of the course lit and headlamps recommended for the unlit stretches.

sections.heading: Lechon at the Aid Stations
paragraphs: Aid stations have featured local delicacies like lechon baka and lechon baboy alongside standard water and energy drinks, a distinctive touch tied to Bohol's Sandugo Festival noted in 2024 coverage. An earlier finisher, writing about the 2013 half marathon on Running Diva PH, confirmed the basics were solid too: "The stations provided ample supply of water and energy drinks." [2]

sections.heading: Growing Field, GPS Tracking
paragraphs: The 2025 edition (its third installment) drew around 4,300 runners and used the TRACX live-tracking app so family and friends could follow participants' progress via GPS -- a modern touch for a race with roots going back over a decade. Start/finish for recent editions has been at BE Grand Resort Bohol in Panglao, with race-kit collection typically held in the days just before the event.

sections.heading: What Past Finishers Flagged
paragraphs: The same 2018 Takbo.ph recap that praised the road surface also noted friction points: "There was no label on which tent to claim the finisher entitlements," [1] and summed up a mixed experience bluntly: "This year's Bohol International Marathon wasn't the run in paradise as I expected it to be." [1] The reviewer added a balanced note, though: "While the race was not perfect, the event has a lot of potential to create an even better running experience for the participants." [1] Much of the more recent online commentary (2024-2025) is promotional event-preview material rather than independent runner reviews, so it's harder to confirm whether those early logistics gaps have been resolved.

sections.heading: Panglao Island as a Destination
paragraphs: Panglao is the southernmost town of Bohol, an island of just over 91 square kilometres shared with the neighbouring town of Dauis, and home to Bohol-Panglao International Airport, which opened in 2018. [3] That airport access makes race-weekend travel straightforward, and pairs a marathon trip with one of the Philippines' best-known beach and diving destinations.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a flat, well-paved course with a distinctly local aid-station touch and a beach-island destination appeals, the Bohol International Marathon on 30 August 2026 is a reasonable pick with a decade-plus track record, even if recent independent feedback is thin. Runners who want ironclad post-race logistics should pack a bit of patience, based on past participant notes about signage gaps.
